requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set's decisions ledger holds an entry for every decision that changes a plants behaviour the ledger already rules on, added as a new numbered entry naming the entry it supersedes, with the earlier entry kept in the ledger marked superseded and the subject it rules on re-stamped with the new resolution, who decided it and the new entry's id.
requirements.why: The ledger is the only place a plants ruling lives, and every conflict entry and every behaviour carries a pointer to it rather than its own answer, so a plants page changed without its entry leaves the set's own record saying the opposite of what the service does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the ledger's 97 entries carry no decision from this programme at all: they settle no content, wording, layout or component question of the design release, name neither the notification list's reframing nor a party picker's page size, and the seven superseded entries were every one of them replaced by the set's own owner rulings (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-005, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-183-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-184). The Copy as new action on the notification view header (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-017) is the first such decision: it supersedes the ledger's park of reusing a previous consignment and the 'minus Copy as new' clause of the post-submission action set, both of which today say plants has no Copy as new.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey specification's entry for each page, obligation and behaviour says what that page, obligation or behaviour does in the service, so a reader of the specification and a user of the journey see the same thing.
requirements.why: The specification is the plants set's contract and the tests linked to its scenarios are its evidence, so an entry that still reads the old way makes the contract false and the evidence point at behaviour nobody has.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the specification states the journey as it stood before this programme: the overview page is headed Overview with four numbered groups and five row statuses, the read-only view carries no Copy as new and a reuse behaviour says there is none, the page order ends at check your answers from the contact page, and the picker, list and status-strip entries describe today's layout (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-019, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-020, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-050, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-067, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-080). It also still marks all seven of its sources as being extracted from one 6 September snapshot, says the whole-journey fixture and the contract-test table do not exist when both do, and holds an empty happy-path fixture beside it (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-010, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-010-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-227, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-228, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-229). It disagrees with itself or the code in four places: a copied banner on the list against no Copy as new on the view, the Address book link pointing at '#' while the layout links the real address book, two Ministry of Justice Frontend versions while the repo pins 12.0.1, and the consignor stored as a copy while the ledger's d-089 says a reference (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-080-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-084-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-118-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-207-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants conflicts register's entry for a recorded disagreement names the decision that settled it, with that decision's resolution and who made it.
requirements.why: The register carries a pointer to the ledger and never its own answer, so an entry left pointing at a withdrawn decision reads as settled when it is not.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all 40 entries point at the set's own panel or owner rulings, 33 to the panel and 7 to the owner, and none of them points at a decision of this programme (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-008, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-009). One entry also contradicts itself: c-011's resolution says the contact number and contact email fields were taken off it, while its field list, and c-025's, still name both (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-120-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants panel's evidence stays as it is when a ruling changes: its eight dockets, its 83 rulings with their rationale, spec changes and dissent, its reconciliation entries, its critic report and its panel README.
requirements.why: They record why each plants decision was taken, so a reopened question starts from the argument rather than the outcome; editing them would rewrite the reasoning instead of adding to it.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's own rule already says that changing a ruling leaves rulings.json and critic.json alone and edits the ledger and its subject in one commit (repo-plantsfrontend-p17-005).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants notification view header offers the same three actions as the live animals header: Amend this notification, Copy as new and Delete. Copy as new posts a form of its own, no action shares another action's form, and Copy as new carries the notification's own plants answers into the new draft.
requirements.why: A trader moving between the two journeys finds the same actions in the same place, and every layer beneath the button (the plants backend's copy endpoint, the frontend's real and stub persistence and the engine's copy) already exists, so only the header action and its route are missing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the plants read-only view's header carries the reference heading, the status tag, the date line, Amend, Delete notification and the import reference numbers, with no Copy as new, and the list offers View, Amend and Delete with no Copy as new anywhere (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-050, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-131, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-027). The copy machinery beneath it is already on main (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-020, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-028).

requirements.statement: A change mirrored into the high-risk plants journey changes its structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and never which questions it asks, which values a field offers or which commodities a rule covers.
requirements.why: The plants journey's data comes from its own statute and policy paper, so a look-and-feel change that moved a question or a value would put the service outside the law it implements.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants set's own standing rulings already say so: the fourth ranks the policy paper and its draft statute above the Confluence pages, the Mural board and the prototype, and the fifth keeps the animals shape only where no plants source gives a reason to diverge (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-004).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants notification's late flag is set once, at its first submission from draft, and the confirmation page, the read-only view and the list card read the stored value; a resubmission after an amendment moves the submitted date and leaves the flag alone, and a cancelled amendment restores the snapshot carrying it.
requirements.why: Lateness is judged against the timing the trader was held to when they first notified, so recomputing it from a later submission would change a recorded fact about a submitted notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants ledger already rules the late flag a stored system value committed immediately before submitting while the notification is a draft, and read back rather than recomputed (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-018, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-025).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page answers a validation failure with HTTP 400, one error summary titled "There is a problem" carrying a link per field error, an "Error:" prefix on the page title, the message beside each field, and the trader's own answers kept.
requirements.why: A trader who gets something wrong sees what to fix without losing what they typed, and the status code tells a monitor the request was refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants already answers every validation failure with a 400 rather than the live animals mixture of 200s (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-072).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is checked for accessibility on its first render and on its validation-error state against the five rule sets covering WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA, failing on any serious or critical violation, and no page narrows that list.
requirements.why: The machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules only run when their tags are asked for, and a page allowed to narrow the list would hide the very rules the service is held to.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants fit harness already builds its check with the five tags, so the ruling and the code agree (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-174).

requirements.statement: Save and return to overview on a high-risk plants page makes the same checks as Save and continue and changes only where a valid save goes.
requirements.why: Two buttons that save the same page must either both accept an answer or both refuse it, or a trader can save past a check by choosing the other button.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants records already describe it that way: Save and return to overview commits the page and opens the overview whichever page it is pressed on, under the same page-level checks as Save and continue (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-061, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-106).

requirements.statement: An answer on a high-risk plants notification that leaves scope is purged and never restored, scope is worked out afresh on every read and write rather than stored, and a page whose every question is out of scope is passed over by Save and continue.
requirements.why: A notification must hold only what its consignment needs, so an answer kept out of sight would be submitted as part of a record the trader was never shown.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants ledger already rules the wipe and the fresh evaluation on every read and write (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-062, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-103).

requirements.statement: The organisation whose address book a high-risk plants picker reads comes only from the verified session, never from the submitted form.
requirements.why: Otherwise a trader could reach another organisation's addresses by posting an identifier.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants specification already records that the organisation is taken only from the verified session (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-079-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the behaviours its own specification records: its entry guard, its one page order, its save-and-return and Back rules, its scope purge, its two-page commodity collection, its own session cookies, its lenient page validation, its four system-populated values, its layout chrome and its boot guards.
requirements.why: They are the platform behaviour every plants page is built on, so a look-and-feel change is made inside them rather than against them.
requirements.deltaNote: The specification's behaviours block already holds all of them (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-060 to repo-plantsfrontend-p15-171), and the entry guard the backlog extras record as inert already redirects to the commodity type page in the code (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-189).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the data, validation and behaviour its own decisions ledger and conflicts register have settled: its commodity vocabulary and lists, the per-category origin narrowing, the per-line fields and their formats, the arrival matters, the identification numbers, the single contact pick, the declaration statements, the reference number, the four-value status vocabulary and the two timing windows.
requirements.why: Those decisions rest on the plants statute and policy paper rather than on any design, so a change made for look and feel leaves them exactly as they are.
requirements.deltaNote: The 97 ledger entries and the 40 register entries already hold these decisions, each subject carrying a pointer to the entry that settled it, and the rulings that describe submission name the same submit step the engine calls (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-009, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-188).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set's own engineering-hygiene increments stay the plants team's work: its continuous-integration parity and workflow fixes, the multi-architecture and non-gating-audit publish changes, the Lighthouse scripts, the dependency-update configuration, the architecture-lint baseline, the removal of the unused platform services, the collection exemplars, the documentation-drift sweep, the unauthorised view's copy and the dashboard's empty submitted date.
requirements.why: The goal is what a user sees in the journeys that exist, and the set's own build hygiene lies outside it; most of these are in any case done in the code since the ledger recorded them (the Lighthouse scripts and workflow, the end-to-end, arm64, concurrency, security-audit, weekly, SonarCloud and FIT workflow changes, and a generated Dependabot configuration that departs from the recorded ESLint policy), and the end-to-end increments' recorded assertions, such as a picker paging at five, are the plants team's to refresh.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants records' structural gaps stay as they are: the conflicts register has no state for an unsettled disagreement, no entry says who may reopen a ruling or on what evidence, the parked questions have no owner and no date, the panel evidence names no judge or chair and does not say which ledger entry each of its rulings became, and three of the five standing rulings are nowhere stated in their own words.
requirements.why: This programme keeps its own open questions and decisions in its own records, and the plants panel's evidence belongs to the work that produced it.

requirements.statement: The questions the high-risk plants set has parked stay parked: users, sign-in models, agents, delegation and plant-operator registration; internal-user login; bulk upload and importing from existing documents; regulator, inspector and analyst screens; list maintenance, risk classification and spot-check scheduling; document uploads; the outbox and event publishing; a combined animals and plants list; competent-authority routing; the notification reference's type-code prefix; the service name, feedback address and helpdesk lines; guidance and a before-you-start page; the previous scheme and the Northern Irish and Irish precedents; the lawful basis, privacy notice and retention period; a live Welsh service; a meaning for "sustainable"; and parity of internal access.
requirements.why: Each waits on a policy answer nobody has or on capability nobody is building, and the goal is the look and feel of the journeys that exist.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area's working set that state one plants page's own content, questions, options, hints or error messages are weighed in that page's area: the commodity type and commodity pages, origin, arrival status and arrival details, place of destination, the consignor and contact pickers, the identification numbers, the overview, check your answers, the declaration, the confirmation, the notification list, and the delete and cancel-amendment pages.
requirements.why: Each page's area reads the same claims against the plants code and the design, and one requirement per difference a user can see belongs there rather than in the record of what the set has settled.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the four decisions its ledger has already landed in the code: no use, contact-number or contact-email obligation and no contact-details page, so the contact section is the one address-book pick; the commodity-type save keeps the lines the new type allows, counts the rest as removed and opens the commodities list with that count; the declaration carries its three plants statements, the last covering failing to notify, notifying late and giving incorrect details; and the arrival-status page asks whether the consignment has arrived in Great Britain.
requirements.why: A change made for the look of a page must not quietly undo a decision the set has already built, and these four are the ones where the ledger and the code have been checked against each other.
requirements.deltaNote: Each was checked against the code and found in place: the obligations manifest holds no use, contact-number or contact-email obligation and there is no contact-details feature folder; the commodity-type controller reconciles and redirects with the removed count; the declaration copy holds the three statements; and the arrival-status copy asks about Great Britain (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-178, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-179, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-180, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-181).

conflicts.about: Whether the high-risk plants notification view header gains a Copy as new action, which the plants set's own records park.

positions.says: The plants header gains Copy as new, so the live animals and plants headers offer the same three actions: Amend this notification, Copy as new and Delete.
The one-form-each header rule covers Amend, Copy as new and Delete on the notification view header, and applies in both the live animals frontend and the plants frontend.
Copy as new is left out of the plants view header because plants has parked it.
Reusing a previous consignment is parked with no increment of its own: it maps onto the animals Copy as new action, left out of the first pass.
A trader cannot reuse a previous notification: there is no Copy as new action and no notification-copied banner.
The animals post-submission action set is in scope minus Copy as new.

conflicts.outcome: The 25 November (b) ruling, which answered this question against its old default, wins: the plants notification view header offers Amend this notification, Copy as new and Delete, as the live animals header does, with Copy as new posting its own form under the 19 November one-form-each rule and carrying plants' own answers. It is wiring only, because the plants backend's copy endpoint and the frontend's persistence and engine copy are already on main, so the plants backend joins nothing. The 9 October afternoon claim that left Copy as new out, the plants ledger's park of reusing a previous consignment and the specification's no-reuse constraint are set aside. The plants ledger's post-submission action set (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-073) is not overruled, because the rest of it, the list actions, the read-only view's Delete and Cancel amendment and the confirmation's view-or-amend block, still stands; only its 'minus Copy as new' clause gives way, and the ledger records that through a new superseding entry. Which state headers carry Copy as new (a draft's as well as a submitted one's) follows the live animals header, which the manage notifications area decides.

conflicts.about: Whether the high-risk plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded is restored, as the set's own convention requires.

positions.says: A ruling changes only through a new numbered entry that supersedes the earlier one, which stays in the ledger marked superseded, and a ruling lives nowhere else.
The plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded stays as it is, and the ruling records no interest in changing it.

conflicts.outcome: The 19 November ruling wins: the deleted plants journey spec ruling is not restored and nothing is added to record its removal. The set's convention is not set aside, because it still governs every entry this programme adds to the ledger, so no claim is overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether the high-risk plants address pickers keep the pagination and the restatement of the chosen address that their own records describe.

positions.says: Pagination is kept everywhere, every picker pages at eight and the restatement of the chosen address comes back, the plants contact picker included.
The plants address pickers lose their pagination and their 'Selected address' inset.
A plants picker shows eight addresses a page with pagination beyond that and an inset naming the address already chosen.

conflicts.outcome: The 25 November ruling wins over the 9 October afternoon claim, which it names as an error: every plants picker pages at eight and keeps the restatement of the chosen address. That is what the plants records already describe, so the plants records stand and the pickers need no ledger entry.
